canonicalExplanation.summary: A classic Java application needs four things to line up. The file **Main.java** contains **`public class Main`**: a public class's name must match the file name exactly, capitals included. The class declares the entry point **`public static void main(String[] args)`**: public so the launcher can call it, static so no object is needed, and `String[] args` for command-line arguments. You compile with **`javac Main.java`**, and run with **`java Main`**, the **class name**, not `Main.class`. Get any piece wrong and you'll see a compile error or "Main method not found". (Java 21+ also has simplified preview forms, but this classic form works everywhere.)

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A learner saves `public class HelloWorld` in a file called hello.java, then runs `java hello.class`. javac complains the class should be declared in HelloWorld.java; after fixing that, java says it can't find the class. Main.java declares public class Main with public static void main(String[] args), prints one line, compiles with javac, and runs with java Main. In this lesson you'll build and explain a minimal Java application from the command line.

examples.title: Main.java, done properly

walkthrough: **Main.java declares public class Main:** file and class names match exactly.
**With public static void main(String[] args), prints one line:** Hello, world!

examples.title: The missing main
examples.situation: A learner renames main to start and gets "Error: Main method not found in class Main".
walkthrough: The launcher only looks for main with the standard signature.
Other methods can be called from main.
examples.result: The program starts at the intended entry point.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Java executes any method named main regardless of its declaring class, modifiers, parameter type, or how the class is launched.
misconceptions.correction: The launcher runs main only in the class you name, and only with the expected signature. Wrong modifiers, parameter types or launch names prevent it from running.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In the opening story, which two names didn't match?

analogy.example: Launching a Java program is like **a courier delivering to a named front door**: the address (class name) must match the house (file and class), and the door must be the standard front door (public static void main). A side door with a different shape isn't recognised.
limitations: Couriers can knock on other doors; the launcher won't.
Arguments are the parcel handed through the door.

recap.summary: To build a minimal Java application, put public class Main in Main.java, declare public static void main(String[] args), compile with javac Main.java, and run with java Main (the class name), passing any arguments after it.
